title: Contraction of an integral in an $L^p$ norm
statement: Let $(alpha,mu)$ and $(beta,nu)$ be measurable spaces with measures, where $mu$ is s-finite and $nu$ is a probability measure. If $1\le p\le\infty$ and $F:\alpha\times\beta\to\mathbb R$ is strongly measurable almost everywhere with respect to $mu\otimesnu$, then the function obtained by integrating $F(x,y)$ over $y$ has $L^p(mu)$ norm at most the $L^p(mu\otimesnu)$ norm of $F$.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to $mu\otimesnu$
